title: An Adaptive and Reconfigurable Robot-Assisted SPECT Imaging System
text:
The overall goal of this project is to develop a novel robot-assisted molecular imaging system for personalized
diagnosis and image-guided therapeutic applications. The robotic system would move a new lightweight imaging
camera around the patient’s body to acquire the most accurate images, adapting to the patient’s anatomy and
needs. This could lead to faster and more precise diagnoses, shorter scan times, and lower radiation exposure,
with the potential to significantly improve medical imaging and patient care.

title: Optical dissection of human embryonic germ layer patterning mechanisms using microengineered stem cell models
text:
A significant number of pregnancies fail at very early stages in embryonic development for reasons that have
been difficult to ascertain due to limitations in studying human development. We propose to investigate the
developmental mechanisms the human embryo uses at these early stages to pattern its initial form through an
innovative combination of micron-scale stem cell engineering technologies and optogenetic tools, that enable
the systematic variation of the signaling patterns thought to drive human embryonic pattern formation. In
addition to understanding these mechanisms, enhanced control of natural patterning mechanisms of human
stem cells promises to boost the efficiency and precision of engineered tissues for regenerative medicine.

title: Resource Section
text:
Resource Section
The Mutant Mouse Resource and Research Center (MMRRC) at UC Davis (MMRRC-UCD) is the flagship of
the MMRRC consortium and serves a leading role in facilitating research by identifying, acquiring, evaluating,
characterizing, cryopreserving, and distributing mutant mouse strains to qualified biomedical investigators. The
MMRRC-UCD ensures that scientifically valuable transgenic, knockout, and other genetically-modified mutant
mice, embryonic stem (ES) cells, hybridomas, mouse tissues, and other relevant biomaterials are maintained
and made available and accessible for investigational use by researchers across the biomedical scientific
community. The MMRRC-UCD provides expertise, infrastructure, resources and services to preserve mouse
strains in perpetuity, protect them from catastrophic loss, mitigate against genetic and phenotypic drift, prevent
pathogenic contamination and disease, add and enhance phenotypic characterization, and conduct resource-
related research to advance, catalyze and accelerate the study of mutant mice as models of human disease.
The MMRRC-UCD fosters and promotes discovery of new diagnostics, treatments, and prevention strategies
against human diseases, optimizes reproducibility of studies, and assures scientific rigor and transparency.

title: Understanding and Manipulating G Protein α Subunit and Phospholipase C Signaling Networks
text:
G protein coupled receptors (GPCRs) are a major class of transmembrane receptors responsible for
recognition of a large class of diverse ligands and are major targets of therapeutic drugs. Here we propose a
comprehensive analysis of mechanisms for GPCR-dependent regulation of downstream signaling processes.
We expect to reveal novel signaling mechanisms with broad implications for GPCR signaling in general, and
new paradigms for adrenergic regulation of cardiac function and failure, that have the potential to drive
development of novel therapeutics.

title: Innate lymphoid Cells Drive Young Onset Lung Cancer Incidences in Females
text:
It is now widely recognized that sexual disparity plays a critical role in cancer progression and immunotherapy
response; however, the mechanisms behind this paradox remain poorly understood. We have identified that
arginine metabolism augments ILC2 immune cell function and is the main driver of LUAD tumorigenesis in
women. Targeting arginine metabolism along with immune checkpoint inhibitors is a potential therapy to
overcome immunotherapy resistance in women with LUAD.

title: Use of Novel Multi-modality Imaging to Evaluate the Relationship Between Sleep Duration, Vascular Inflammation, and Visceral Adiposity
text:
Chronic sleep deprivation is a crisis and growing epidemic both nationally and globally, the cardiovascular
consequences of which need further investigation according to the American Heart Association. This proposal
aims to investigates both short sleep duration and sleep irregularity as potentially modifiable risk factors for
vascular inflammation and visceral adiposity (a known contributor to cardiometabolic disease risk) measured
using novel, multi-modality imaging. The long-term goal is for Dr. Kundel to become a successful independent
investigator in sleep research, elucidating mechanistic pathways linking sleep deprivation to cardiovascular
disease, and developing preventative strategies and therapeutic interventions (i.e., sleep extension trials) to gain
deeper insights into mechanisms by which sleep modulates inflammation.

title: Time-varying spatiotemporal causal interactions in the functional brain networks
text:
Project Narratives
This project aims to develop a novel computational paradigm for comprehensively characterizing and interpreting
the causal system and its variability in functional brain networks. The findings will be translated in clinical studies
of patients with different severity of neurological disorders to guide therapeutic practices, and particularly, post-
concussive vestibular impairment syndrome will be used as one illustrative example in this study. Upon
conclusion, we will understand the information transfer in resting state brain networks as well as its role in
differentiating the subtypes of vestibular impairment.

title: Mapping neural targets and advancing neuromodulation techniques for disorders of consciousness
text:
Utilizing advanced neuroimaging and machine learning to investigate subcortical arousal in auditory
perception holds promise for improved detection of perceptual awareness, laying the groundwork for
potential therapeutic interventions in severe brain disorders and anesthesia, when explicit reporting is
challenging. Exploring non- invasive neuromodulation strategies for disorders of consciousness contributes
to the development of novel therapeutic approaches, holding the potential to enhance health by offering a
widely applicable intervention for patients with limited options for behavioral recovery following severe brain
injuries.

title: Development of ST2 Nanobodies for Colorectal Cancer Immunotherapy
text:
Lay Narrative
Immunotherapy has advanced the treatment of cancer, but in colon rectal cancer, a leading cancer among
both men and women, cure rates remain low. Therefore, additional therapeutic and diagnostic options are
needed for novel targets. This study will establish the essential basics leading to potential clinical translation for
ST2 as target for cancer treatment. We will assess its potential using single domain antibodies, referred to as
nanobodies and will also assess its therapeutic using intratumoral mRNA encoding for anti-ST2 nanobodies.

title: Tourette Syndrome genetics and neuroimaging international collaborative study
text:
Tourette Syndrome (TS) is a complex disorder, for which there is no cure and efforts to develop novel treatments
are hampered by our limited understanding of the neurobiology and brain structural and functional deficits that
underlie the disorder. TS is also highly heterogeneous and often comorbid with Obsessive Compulsive Disorder
(OCD), Attention Deficit and Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), Major Depressive
Disorder (MDD), and Anxiety Disorder (AXD), further complicating our efforts. Leveraging ties to ENIGMA and
an international network of collaborators, we will pursue the largest neuroimaging and genetics studies for TS to
date, pooling, harmonizing and jointly analyzing worldwide datasets for TS and highly comorbid disorders
shedding light into TS neurobiology and identifying biomarkers that could help tailor individualized management
approaches.

title: Examining Barriers to Lung Cancer Screening
text:
Lung cancer screening helps to identify early-stage lung cancer when it is less costly and more curable,
however participation in lung cancer screening programs is far below rates for other types of preventive cancer
screenings, particularly in minority populations. Barriers to lung cancer screening participation are poorly
understood, creating challenges in identifying and intervening for individuals at elevated risk of not receiving
screening. Findings from this study can equip healthcare systems with actionable evidence to conduct
outreach efforts and implement cost-effective interventions aimed at enhancing LCS participation and
adherence, while reducing screening disparities.

title: Novel 3D Quantitative Dynamic MRI to Characterize Obstructive Sleep Apnea
text:
Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is the most common type of sleep related breathing disorder characterized by
frequent airway collapse during sleep. The goal of the project is to develop an innovative motion robust 3D
high resolution dynamic MRI approach to quantitatively discern airway shaping in OSA. The successful
completion will overcome major technical challenges in safely quantitating airway collapse during OSA in
sleep.

title: Defining Relationships of Early Mediators and Moderators of Sleep (DREAMS)
text: Sleep health is essential for well-being, yet significant problems exist for young children (2-5 years old) living with limited resources. The objective of this research is to understand problems in early sleep health by examining how neighborhood, family, and child factors predict children’s sleep health. This study will provide a critical next step in reducing problems in early childhood sleep health and its downstream effects.

title: Precision Metabolic Risk Stratification in Depression via Multi-Omics and EHR
text:
Major depressive disorder (MDD) is an underrecognized risk factor for type 2 diabetes (T2D), yet existing risk
prediction tools have not been validated in this high-risk population. Leveraging large-scale health system
biobanks, this project will validate multi-omics risk scores for T2D in patients with MDD, characterize SSRI-
induced metabolic sensitivity through EHR-based biomarker discovery, and develop transparent risk
stratification models for T2D at the time of MDD diagnosis in real-world clinical settings. These findings will
establish the scientific foundation for metabolic monitoring guidelines and precision T2D prevention strategies
in psychiatric populations.

title: Decoding the Mechanism of Pathogenic Enhancer Mutations In Congenital Limb Disorders
text:
Increasing evidence links a range of disorders, from congenital malformations to autism, intellectual disability,
and brain tumors, to mutations that cause genes to be erroneously activated. Called gain-of-function mutations,
such alterations often affect regions of our genomes called enhancers—“switches” for gene activity. The
proposed research will use limb development as a model to determine the molecular mechanism by which these
gain-of-function enhancer mutations promote limb congenital malformations utilizing novel genetically
engineered mice and cutting-edge genomics and imaging methods.
.

title: Mental Health Assessment and Technology Research Core
text: Despite increasing rates of pediatric mental health concerns, many research teams lack the infrastructure, tools, and training to implement rigorous, developmentally appropriate assessments essential for valid and impactful research. The Mental Health Assessment and Technology Research Core (MHAT-RC), originally launched in Phase I as the Pediatric Biopsychology Core, was created to address this critical gap. Over the past four years, MHAT-RC has built foundational infrastructure and provided expert consultation to support state-of-the-science mental health assessments, including validated questionnaires, ecological momentary assessment (EMA), psychophysiological monitoring, and electronic health record (EHR) data integration. These services have reached over 40 investigators, contributed to over 200 peer- reviewed publications, and helped launch multiple NIH-funded projects. In Phase II, MHAT-RC will expand its services, infrastructure, and sustainability efforts to meet growing institutional demand and advance the scientific rigor of child and adolescent mental health research. Specifically, the Core will: (1) maintain and expand centralized services to support developmentally appropriate, evidence-based assessments; (2) enhance access to technology-enabled assessment methods and EHR data integration; and (3) develop infrastructure and consultation services to support the harmonization and analysis of complex, multimodal data streams. These services will be delivered in close collaboration with other institutional cores and guided by a structured business plan that transitions the Core to a fee-for-service model while maintaining prioritized support for COBRE Project Leaders and early-career investigators. By expanding access to scalable, technology-enhanced assessments and analytic tools, MHAT-RC will empower investigators to answer pressing questions in pediatric mental health with increased precision, reproducibility, and translational relevance. Through a combination of expert consultation, reusable infrastructure, and training, Phase II will cement MHAT-RC’s role as a critical and sustainable research resource at Bradley Hospital and across IDeA-state institutions.

title: Mechanism of Manganese-induced neurotoxicity via microglial Leucine Rich Repeat Kinase 2 (LRRK2)
text:
Chronic exposure to elevated manganese (Mn) levels causes a neurological disease, but the mechanism for
Mn-induced neurotoxicity is yet to be established. Parkinson’s disease (PD)-related gene Leucine-Rich Repeat
Kinase 2 (LRRK2) appears to play a critical role in Mn-induced neurotoxicity, possibly by Mn-induced LRRK2
hyper-kinase activity, which is further exacerbated in G2019S mutated LRRK2 in microglia, suggesting that the
LRRK2 hyper-kinase activity could be a pivotal toxicity mechanism of Mn-induced neurotoxicity. Thus, the current
proposal will investigate the comprehensive neurotoxic mechanisms involved in Mn-induced LRRK2 hyper-
kinase activity, and its cellular and molecular targets for the development of therapeutic strategies to treat Mn
toxicity as well as neurological disorders associated with hyper-LRRK2 kinase activity.

title: Administrative, Biostatistics, Data Management, and Bioinformatics Core
text: Summary The Administrative, Biostatistics, Data Management & Bioinformatics Core is essential for the smooth functioning of the overall Program Project. Core A has three major functions: First, the Core will provide supervision of program finances, administrative and secretarial support, maintenance of authorizations and adherence to institutional requirements, and coordination of meetings of the Program Project team and the Internal and External Advisory Boards. Second, the Core will provide data management and Biostatistics support for the Program Project. Third, the Core will provide Bioinformatics support for the Program Project. All components of this Core will serve each of the three Projects over all five years of the Program Project.

title: Bile acid-mediated control of lipid absorption and fatty liver disease
text:
Relevance to Public Health
NALFD/NASH are the leading cause of chronic liver disease in the US, and therefore creates a significant burden
to the national health system and there are limited options for treatments. Our discovery that altering bile acid
selectively changes the absorption of different fatty acids will advance our fundamental understanding of how
our bodies take up lipids from the diet, which is a significant contributor to NAFLD to NASH, and may reveal
novel opportunities for therapeutic intervention.

title: Improving hand kinematic predictions from implanted EMG in humans and monkeys
text:
Our overall objective is to fully understand how to take high quality muscle signals from
implanted electrodes and predict the position and movement of the hand and fingers. This is
very important for people with upper limb amputations for controlling their prosthetic hand, but
could also impact our understanding of how to control other complex robotic systems.
